findings.description: The PR adds SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0 to build configurations that retain SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = minimal. The compiler flag -strict-concurrency=minimal overrides Swift 6's default complete concurrency checking, so the Firefox, FirefoxStaging, and FirefoxBeta configurations compile with Swift 6 language mode but only minimal Sendable/isolation diagnostics. Failure: a data race introduced in Client code is not diagnosed when building these configurations; it ships and can crash or corrupt state at runtime. The same pairing occurs at lines 27951, 27991, 29779, 29816, 30430, and 30467 (all six configuration blocks that pair SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = minimal with the new SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0). Fix: set SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete (or remove the override) wherever SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0 is set.
findings.failureMode: Swift 6 data-race diagnostics are silently disabled in the main app build configurations, so concurrency defects compile cleanly and reach production.
findings.title: Swift 6 enabled under minimal concurrency checking

findings.description: Wrapping onboardingService.handleAction in Task { } makes previously-synchronous completion callbacks (e.g. .forwardOneCard → .advance(1)) asynchronous. Failure: user taps "Next" then quickly taps "Later"; skipOnboarding() runs immediately and calls onComplete → parentCoordinator.didFinishLaunch (which does router.dismiss, remove(child:), and startBrowser). The deferred Task then runs, calls completion(.advance), and advanceFromCard on the last card calls onComplete again → didFinishLaunch again → double router.dismiss, double remove(child:), double startBrowser. Fix: call handleAction directly (it is @MainActor and synchronous) instead of wrapping it in Task.
findings.failureMode: Concurrent "Next" and "Later" taps cause didFinishLaunch to run twice, producing double dismissal, double child removal, and double browser start.
findings.title: Task wrap defers onboarding completion and races with skip

findings.description: The diff deletes the nested struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 } and replaces UX.buttonSize with the magic number 40 at the close-button height/width constraints (lines 192–193). AGENTS.md Rule 13 requires UI measurement constants to live in a nested UX struct. Failure: repository compliance check for Rule 13 fails; UI constants are scattered as literals instead of a dedicated UX namespace. Fix: restore a nested UX struct and reference UX.buttonSize (or equivalent) from the constraint sites.
findings.failureMode: AGENTS.md Rule 13 compliance failure: UI layout constants appear as raw literals instead of nested UX struct members.
findings.title: UI constant inlined after UX struct deletion

findings.description: Changes `"strict": true` to `"strict": false` in tsconfig.app.json. AGENTS.md mandate #11 requires strict mode enabled (failure criteria: "TypeScript strict mode is disabled or type checking is not part of the validation pipeline"). Verified impact: with `strict: true` `tsc -b --noEmit` reports 0 errors; with `strict: false` it reports 242 errors, including 47 TanStack Router type assertions that fail with `"strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json"`. The required CI Build job runs `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`), so `tsc -b` fails and the ui-v2 build breaks on every PR. `validate:types` (`tsc -b --noEmit`) fails identically. Failure scenario: any ui-v2 PR (including this one) fails the Build CI job; the UI cannot be built or type-validated, and strict-mode checks (strictNullChecks etc.) are removed from the whole app so future type errors compile silently.
findings.failureMode: Weakened compile-time type enforcement across ui-v2; type errors that would fail `validate:types`/build now ship to runtime
findings.title: Disables TypeScript strict mode, violating repo mandate

findings.description: WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields binds the Status select to `trigger.expect` (line 37) regardless of posture. Sibling components in the same PR (DeploymentStatusTriggerFields line 31) and the established FlowRunStateTriggerFields pattern switch to `trigger.after` for Proactive ("states to stay in") and `trigger.expect` for Reactive ("states to enter"). Per EventTrigger semantics (`after` = events that must first be seen; Proactive fires on _absence_ of `expect` events within `within`), writing the selected status to `expect` for Proactive inverts the trigger. Failure scenario: user selects Work pool status, sets posture Proactive ("Stays in"), picks status "Not Ready". The value is stored in `expect` and `after` stays empty. The saved automation fires when `prefect.work-pool.not-ready` does NOT occur within `within` — the inverse of "stays in Not Ready".
findings.failureMode: Proactive work-pool status automation gets inverted semantics (fires on absence of the selected status instead of on staying in it)
findings.title: Work-pool Proactive status writes to trigger.expect instead of trigger.after

findings.description: WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields binds the Status select to `trigger.expect` (line 37) regardless of posture — identical defect to work-pool. Sibling DeploymentStatusTriggerFields and FlowRunStateTriggerFields switch to `trigger.after` for Proactive. Failure scenario: user selects Work queue status, posture Proactive ("Stays in"), status "Paused". Value is written to `expect`, `after` remains empty. Per EventTrigger semantics the saved Proactive automation fires when `prefect.work-queue.paused` is absent within `within`, the inverse of "stays in Paused".
findings.failureMode: Proactive work-queue status automation gets inverted semantics (fires on absence of the selected status instead of on staying in it)
findings.title: Work-queue Proactive status writes to trigger.expect instead of trigger.after

findings.description: The onChange handler does `e.target.value.split("\n")` then `field.onChange(lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined)`. `String.split` always returns at least one element (verified: `''.split('\n') === ['']`), so the `undefined` branch is dead code. Failure scenario: user types an event name into Expected Events then deletes it (or presses Enter after the last line). Clearing stores `[""]` instead of leaving `expect` unset; a trailing newline stores `["<event>", ""]`; a blank line between events stores an empty string entry. `['']` passes the zod schema (`z.array(z.string()).optional()`). On the backend `expects()` uses `matches("", event)` (exact equality) so no real event name equals `""`; a Reactive trigger with `expect: ['']` never fires, while the UI displayed an empty field implying no event filter. Trailing/blank lines similarly inject empty event names into the saved automation.
findings.failureMode: Empty or trailing-newline input in Expected Events stores empty-string entries in trigger.expect, producing a never-firing or misconfigured automation
findings.title: Custom textarea split always yields entries; empty strings leak into trigger.expect

findings.description: Work-pool Threshold onChange (line 78) is `field.onChange(parseInt(e.target.value))` while every other threshold/within field in this PR and in FlowRunStateTriggerFields uses `Number(e.target.value)`. `parseInt(\"2.5\")` silently stores 2 and `parseInt(\"1e2\")` stores 1 (stops at `e`), whereas `Number` yields 2.5 and 100. Also `parseInt(\"\")` yields NaN which React may render as \"NaN\" in the controlled number input, unlike `Number(\"\")` yielding 0. Failure scenario: user enters 2.5 (or pastes scientific notation like `1e2`) into the work-pool Threshold input; the form stores a truncated/wrong integer different from the entered value and from what sibling components store, so the saved automation uses a different threshold than the one shown in the UI.
findings.failureMode: Work-pool threshold silently truncates decimals and misparses scientific notation, storing a value different from what the user typed
findings.title: Work-pool threshold uses parseInt, diverging from Number() in all sibling fields

findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 13 requires UI measurement constants to live in a nested UX struct and forbids scattering them as literals. This hunk deletes `struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }` and replaces `UX.buttonSize` with the bare literal `40` at the closeButton height/width constraints (both sites in this array). Failure: the compliance check for rule 13 fails on this UI component because the close-button size is now an unexplained magic number instead of a named UX constant; a later size change must hunt literals instead of one named site. Fix: restore a nested UX constant (e.g. `private struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }`) and reference it from both constraints.
findings.failureMode: Compliance failure: AGENTS.md rule 13 violation — UI measurement literals at lines 192-193 instead of a nested UX constant
findings.title: DownloadToast drops UX struct and inlines magic button size

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>, and prepare_tools (returning crate::Result) uses `?` on it at several call sites (lines 232, 239, 245, 251, 259). crate::Error has no From<FileWriteError> impl (only #[from] io::Error and other unrelated types). A faithful standalone repro of this exact signature and `?` site fails with E0277: the trait From<FileWriteError> is not implemented for Error.
findings.failureMode: cargo check/build of tauri-bundler fails to compile prepare_tools at the write_and_make_executable `?` sites.
findings.title: FileWriteError cannot convert into crate::Error via `?`

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now chmods first and writes second (base wrote first, then chmod). std::fs::set_permissions on a missing path returns NotFound (Os code 2), so creating any new tool file fails with ENOENT before the bytes are written. Affects AppRun, linuxdeploy, gstreamer plugin, and the appimage plugin on first download.
findings.failureMode: First-time prepare_tools with an empty cache: download succeeds, then set_permissions(AppRun-*) returns ENOENT and the `?` aborts bundling.
findings.title: set_permissions runs before fs::write on a not-yet-created file

findings.description: Condition changed from `if !gtk.exists()` to `if gtk.exists()`, so the inlined GTK plugin script is written only when the file is already present and is never created on a fresh tools cache. linuxdeploy is always invoked with `--plugin gtk` (mod.rs ~line 206), so a first-run/empty-cache bundle cannot install the plugin that this PR exists to inline.
findings.failureMode: On an empty tools cache the bundled gtk script is never written; linuxdeploy then cannot find `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk` and AppImage bundling fails (or silently omits GTK).
findings.title: Inverted gtk plugin install condition

findings.description: With set -e, both cache post-process steps run sed -i unconditionally on immodules.cache and loaders.cache. The immediately preceding branches only warn when those files are missing (query tool absent and nothing copied from the host), so sed then fails and aborts the plugin. Same correction at both sites: run sed only when the cache exists.
findings.failureMode: Host without gtk-query-immodules-3.0 or gdk-pixbuf-query-loaders and without a pre-existing cache in the GTK/gdk-pixbuf libdirs: the warning prints, then sed -i ENOENTs and the gtk plugin exits non-zero, failing AppImage bundling.
findings.title: sed runs on missing immodules/loaders caches and aborts under set -e

findings.description: In the GSTREAMER_VERSION=0.10 branch the hook exports GST_PLUGIN_SYSTEM_PATH_0_10 and scanner/helper paths under gstreamer-1.0 / gstreamer1.0, but the same script copies plugins to usr/lib/gstreamer-0.10 and helpers to usr/lib/gstreamer0.10/gstreamer-0.10. The 0.10 bundle looks in empty/wrong dirs.
findings.failureMode: With GSTREAMER_VERSION=0.10 the generated AppRun hook exports wrong plugin/helper paths, so GStreamer 0.10 plugins are not loaded at runtime.
findings.title: GStreamer 0.10 AppRun hook points at 1.0 plugin/helper paths

findings.description: AGENTS.md mandate 8 requires custom error enums to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] with #[error(...)] attributes. FileWriteError implements Display and std::error::Error by hand.
findings.failureMode: Repository compliance failure: custom error type bypasses the mandated thiserror structured-error pattern.
findings.title: FileWriteError hand-implements Display/Error instead of thiserror

findings.description: AGENTS.md mandate 3 requires cargo fmt --check to pass. rustfmt --check on the changed file reports a diff at the new fs::set_permissions(...).map_err(...) line, which exceeds the project max_width and must be wrapped. cargo fmt --all -- --check will fail.

findings.description: show_usage documents GSTREAMER_INCLUDE_BAD_PLUGINS (default disabled), but the script never reads that variable. The copy loop copies every file from the plugins directory, so bad plugins are always bundled and the documented switch is a no-op.
findings.failureMode: User leaves the documented default (bad plugins excluded) or sets GSTREAMER_INCLUDE_BAD_PLUGINS=0/empty; the AppImage still ships every GStreamer plugin including bad ones.
findings.title: GSTREAMER_INCLUDE_BAD_PLUGINS documented but never applied

findings.description: After `Action.SelectLightTheme` (which taps `lightThemeView` per registerSettingsNavigation.swift:117-118), the test reads `darkThemeView`.value into `lightIsSelected` and asserts it equals "1". Base used `lightThemeView`; this is a copy-paste from the Dark block below.

findings.description: In CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer.render_template, `rendered = result.get("result")` is only rejected when it is non-None and non-str (`if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)`). When the executor mapping omits "result" or sets it to None, the function returns None while annotated `-> str`. basedpyright (strict) reports `Type "str | None" is not assignable to return type "str"` at template_renderer.py:40. Callers then do `len(rendered)` in TemplateTransformNode._run, raising TypeError instead of TemplateRenderError. Trigger: CodeExecutor.execute_workflow_code_template (or an injected code_executor) returns a mapping without a string "result". Wrong outcome: `make type-check` fails; at runtime the node fails with TypeError("object of type 'NoneType' has no len()") rather than a TemplateRenderError failure result. Fix: reject None (`if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError(...)`) or coerce/raise before return.
findings.failureMode: make type-check fails on template_renderer.py:40; runtime TypeError in _run when result.get("result") is None
findings.title: render_template can return None despite -> str

Fix the require to `../../lib/magic-link/MagicLink` (or rename the target file and update those other callers).
findings.failureMode: Ghost startup/members API init throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND and crashes before serving requests.
findings.title: Require path magic-link does not resolve

findings.description: The rewrite of the require block removed the trailing semicolons that the base had on these statements (e.g. base `const {Router} = require('express');` became `const {Router} = require('express')`). Affected changed lines: 1-4 and 6-10 (`const {Router}`, `body`, `errors`, `logging`, `PaymentsService`, `TokenService`, `GeolocationService`, `MemberBREADService`, `MemberRepository`). This violates AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule 19 (Code Must Always Use Semicolons): statements must end with explicit semicolons and must not rely on ASI. Restore the semicolons.
findings.failureMode: Repository mandate 19 violated on nine changed statements; code now relies on ASI.
findings.title: Dropped semicolons on require statements

findings.description: Extraction of `original_identifier` was changed from `config.get("identifier")` to `config.get("bundle")`. The app identifier lives at the top-level `identifier` key (config.schema.json property `identifier`); `"bundle"` is an object (BundleConfig), so `id.as_str()` is `None` and `original_identifier` is always `None`. Failure: `read_options` in crates/tauri-cli/src/mobile/mod.rs builds `format!("{}-server-addr", config.original_identifier().context("app configuration is missing an identifier")?)` then `.expect("failed to read CLI options")`, so every `android-studio-script` / `xcode-script` invocation panics. `write_options` returns the same error and never writes the addr file. `find_bundle_identifier_overwriter` still reads `"identifier"`, confirming the key rename is unintended.
findings.failureMode: original_identifier is always None (config.get("bundle") is an object, not a string); read_options panics with "failed to read CLI options" on every mobile IDE build script despite a valid identifier in tauri.conf.json.
findings.title: original_identifier reads config key "bundle" instead of "identifier"

findings.description: The schema-validation gate was changed from `||` to `&&` between the `"json"` and `"json5"` extension checks. A path can never have both extensions at once, so the body is dead and `config_schema_validator().iter_errors(...)` is never invoked. Failure: a `tauri.conf.json` or `tauri.conf.json5` with an invalid field or type no longer logs schema errors and no longer calls `exit(1)` in non-reload mode; invalid configs proceed to `serde_json::from_value` and surface as opaque parse errors or wrong runtime behaviour instead of schema diagnostics. The replacement may exist outside the visible diff, but nothing visible re-establishes the guard.
findings.failureMode: Invalid tauri.conf.json/json5 that would have been rejected by schema validation now silently passes the schema gate; errors are missing or reduced to deserialization failures.
findings.title: Schema validation condition uses && instead of || so it never runs

findings.description: Previously `merge_with` deserialized the merged `value` back into `config_metadata.inner`. The new code builds `value`, calls `merge(&mut value, &merge_config)`, then drops `value` and only records `merge_config` in `extensions`. Failure: a caller that invokes `merge_with` with `{"build":{"devUrl":"http://localhost:3000"}}` and then reads the ConfigHandle via Deref still sees the old `build.dev_url`; the documented contract ("merges the loaded config with the given value") is not met. Visible callers crate::helpers::config::merge_with in android_studio_script.rs and xcode_script.rs pass `--config` overrides expecting them to apply.
findings.failureMode: merge_with discards the merged JSON and leaves inner unchanged; later reads of the ConfigHandle ignore the merged overrides.
findings.title: merge_with no longer writes merged value back into config_metadata.inner

findings.description: AGENTS.md mandate 3 requires `cargo fmt --all -- --check` to pass with rustfmt.toml `max_width = 100`. The new `config_schema_validator` line 153 is 156 characters (`serde_json::from_str(...).expect(\"Failed to parse config schema bundled in the tauri-cli\")`), which rustfmt must wrap. Failure: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` reports the file needs formatting and the format gate fails.
findings.failureMode: Line 153 is 156 chars against max_width=100; cargo fmt --check fails on crates/tauri-cli/src/helpers/config.rs.
findings.title: New OnceLock schema init line exceeds rustfmt max_width

findings.description: The diff updates displayName to "Use XCode 16.4.0" on both macOS jobs (lines 167 and 393), but the actual command `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` is unchanged at lines 166 and 392. Combined with the pool image change from macOS-13 to macOS-15, the step either fails because Xcode 15.2.0 is absent on the new image, or silently uses the wrong Xcode version contradicting the declared intent. Fix: update the xcode-select path to /Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app/Contents/Developer at both sites.
findings.failureMode: macOS CI job fails at xcode-select if Xcode_15.2.0.app is not installed on macOS-15, or builds with Xcode 15.2.0 instead of the intended 16.4.0 causing toolchain mismatch.
findings.title: XCode path still selects 15.2.0 while displayName claims 16.4.0

findings.description: ValidateBaseline changed from true to false. Packaging.targets EnsureBaselineIsUpdated requires ValidateBaseline=='true' AND IsServicingBuild=='true' to enforce AspNetCoreBaselineVersion==PreviousAspNetCoreReleaseVersion. Current AspNetCoreBaselineVersion is 9.0.0 (eng/Baseline.Designer.props) but PreviousAspNetCoreReleaseVersion is 10.0.0 (AspNetCorePatchVersion=1). Disabling validation hides this two-major-version gap so the build proceeds with 9.0.0 BaselinePackageReference items for a 10.0.1 servicing build, causing BUILD002 and reference resolution to compare against the wrong baseline.
findings.failureMode: Build succeeds with AspNetCoreBaselineVersion != PreviousAspNetCoreReleaseVersion because EnsureBaselineIsUpdated is disabled. Out-of-date baselines ship without detection.
findings.title: ValidateBaseline disabled, bypassing EnsureBaselineIsUpdated enforcement

findings.description: The BUILD002 error that prevents package reference removals in servicing updates now requires `'$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1'`. Previously it fired for all servicing builds. For AspNetCorePatchVersion 2 or later, the check is bypassed and a breaking package reference removal can ship in a servicing update without triggering BUILD002. The error text still says "not allowed in a servicing update" implying it should apply to all patches.
findings.failureMode: When building AspNetCorePatchVersion 2 or later with IsServicingBuild true and removed baseline package references, the BUILD002 error does not fire and the build succeeds despite a potential breaking change in a servicing update.
findings.title: BUILD002 enforcement narrowed to only AspNetCorePatchVersion 1

findings.description: PreReleaseVersionLabel is 'servicing' but PreReleaseBrandingLabel conditions only handle 'alpha', 'preview', 'rc', and 'rtm'. Comment says it is 'automatically calculated based on PreReleaseVersionLabel' yet 'servicing' is omitted. PreReleaseBrandingLabel remains empty, producing PackageBrandingVersion like '10.0.1 Build 10.0.1-servicing.xxxxx' in installer ProductName and BundleNameShort without a version label.
findings.failureMode: Build artifacts branded with empty PreReleaseBrandingLabel instead of a 'servicing' label, producing incorrect package/installer version branding.
findings.title: PreReleaseBrandingLabel has no case for 'servicing' despite PreReleaseVersionLabel being 'servicing'

findings.description: The diff converts from file-scoped `namespace ...;` to block-scoped `namespace ... { }` with closing brace at end of file. AGENTS.md rule 2 mandates file-scoped namespace declarations. The new code uses traditional namespace braces at lines 16-17, violating the stated failure criteria.
findings.failureMode: Compliance violation of AGENTS.md rule 2: C# files must use file-scoped namespace syntax (namespace declaration ending with semicolon without braces).
findings.title: Block-scoped namespace violates mandatory file-scoped namespace rule

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction changed displayView from `.readerMode` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. Tapping the reader-mode toolbar button (and VoiceOver magic tap) dispatches GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode, which now yields `.readerModeLongPressAction`. BVC maps that to toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which adds the page to the reading list, instead of toggleReaderMode(). Nothing else produces DisplayType `.readerMode`, so reader mode can no longer be toggled from the toolbar.
findings.failureMode: Tap reader-mode button (or accessibilityPerformMagicTap) on any page: instead of enabling/disabling reader mode, the page is added to the reading list and an a11y announcement is posted. Reader mode toggle is unreachable from this path.
findings.title: showReaderMode now routes to add-to-reading-list instead of toggling reader mode

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry now maps `.available` to `false` and `default` to `true`, inverting isReaderModeEnabled. The comment on the same line still says "will be enabled after action gets executed", matching the previous `.available: true` mapping. Every reader-mode button tap now records the opposite of whether reader mode is being opened or closed.
findings.failureMode: Tap reader-mode button while reader mode is available (about to open): telemetry records enabled=false. Tap while reader mode is active (about to close): telemetry records enabled=true. Wrong Glean extras on every tap.
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry enabled flag inverted

findings.description: cancelEditMode changed `url = (currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL) ? url : nil` to `(currentURL.isWebPage() || currentURL.isReaderModeURL) ? url : nil`. Reader-mode URLs (about:reader?url=...) are web pages and isReaderModeURL, so they were previously discarded and now pass through. handleCancelEditAction then uses this raw internal URL as AddressBarState.url instead of falling back to the prior state.url (the display URL).
findings.failureMode: While a page is open in reader mode, tap the address bar then cancel edit: AddressBarState.url becomes about:reader?url=https://... instead of the decoded/display URL, so the address bar shows the internal reader-mode URL. Previously the action carried url=nil and the reducer fell back to state.url.
findings.title: cancelEdit now keeps raw reader-mode URL in address bar state

findings.description: `private let gleanWrapper` became `let gleanWrapper`, dropping the explicit access modifier required by AGENTS.md rule 11 ("All properties and methods have explicit access control modifiers") and widening an implementation detail from private to implicit internal. Every peer telemetry type keeps this property `private`. No caller reads the property (tests inject via init), so the widening is unnecessary.
findings.failureMode: Repository mandate 11 violation: property that should be private now lacks an explicit access modifier and is module-visible. Observable impact limited to API surface/compliance.
findings.title: gleanWrapper access widened from private; AGENTS.md rule 11 violation

findings.description: Loop condition `j <= keys_result->numkeys` iterates one past valid indices (0..numkeys-1). On the final iteration it reads `keys_result->keys[numkeys]` out of bounds and writes `slot_buffer[numkeys]` out of bounds (buffer allocated for `numkeys` ints at line 1110). For numkeys < MAX_KEYS_BUFFER (6), keys points to the zero-initialized keysbuf, so keys[numkeys].pos == 0 and argv[0] (the command name) is hashed and compared with the real key's slot — almost always differing — causing a spurious CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT return that rejects valid commands. For numkeys >= 6, keys[numkeys] reads past the array entirely (heap or struct tail), yielding a garbage argv index. Trigger: any call with numkeys >= 1 in cluster mode (e.g. SET foo bar via preprocessCommand->extractKeysAndSlot, or getSlotFromCommand in cluster_asm.c). Consequence: heap corruption, crash, or valid single-key commands rejected as cross-slot.
findings.failureMode: Buffer overflow / out-of-bounds memory access on every invocation with keys
findings.title: Off-by-one loop causes OOB read/write in extractSlotFromKeysResult

findings.description: extractSlotFromKeysResult allocates with malloc() and frees with free(), violating repository mandate #2 requiring zmalloc/zcalloc/zrealloc/ztrycalloc/ztrymalloc for all dynamic allocations in src/ and zfree for deallocations. Additionally, malloc's return value is not checked for NULL: on OOM the subsequent store `slot_buffer[j] = this_slot` dereferences NULL and crashes. Using zmalloc (which never returns NULL) would fix both the mandate violation and the crash risk. The allocated slot_buffer is never read after being written — it is dead code whose only effect is the allocation itself and the OOB write described in the off-by-one finding. Trigger: any call with numkeys > 0 in cluster mode. Consequence: memory tracking bypassed; potential NULL dereference crash on OOM.
findings.failureMode: Repository mandate violation: direct malloc/free in src/ bypasses zmalloc tracking
findings.title: Uses malloc/free instead of zmalloc/zfree
